summary.intent: Win the Lio 'Keep the Line Running' hackathon challenge: analyze Soony's confidential launch data, find hidden supply risks, and build a general, adaptable agent product (poller, extraction, recompute, act with human approval) with a polished UI, interview prep and a pitch.
summary.outcome: Found the real launch risks (overbooked art-book receipt, failed statue lot, game-card shortfall, sleeve revision conflict, false magnet alarm), built the Lighthouse product with 360 passing tests, and polished the UI (case flow 'How we got here', Routines fixes, phone layout, top bar). Most work is committed on main but not pushed, live not restarted, and the hand-in was 10 minutes away.

repo: Portal API has only three endpoints (files list, single file, archive.zip) and no webhook or notification, so new drops must be detected by polling the file list and comparing SHA-256 checksums; files are replaced under the same name.
Confidential portal data, scans, notes and .env live in the gitignored data/ folder; .env.example is committed with an empty SOONY_PORTAL_TOKEN.
The team workflow is in CLAUDE.md and PROGRESS.md; each person claims a 'Now' line in PROGRESS.md.
The API server does not load .env on import, so settings like ASK_VIEWER_TITLE need a helper that loads .env first or they are missing after restart.

Routine steps are only valid for certain watched kinds: 'Chase once if no answer' needs routines watching messages awaiting reply, 'Ask for a status' needs shipments; the server rejects others ("step 2 cannot be done on open decisions").
Routines code calls Claude (claude-opus-5-5) with the key from .env independent of ASK_LLM_PROVIDER, so it works on the demo.
Case flow reuses the routine diagram's connector and node components exported from FlowGraph.tsx so the two stay visually consistent.
Demo and live serve the same rebuilt web build; new backend endpoints need a server restart to work, and previews should run on a copy of demo state with background off and email record-only.

Lucas's new-approach branch contains a separate pulse-console app with its own server, inbox and email sending that bypasses the duplicate-send guard and record-only mode, so it should not be merged wholesale.

code.finding: New component rendering the 'How we got here' flow (Portal, Reader, Verifier, Prediction, Approval rule, Decision, Then) from each case's own data; steps missing in the data are omitted, and it was switched from a two-column snake to a single column because the right-to-left second row was confusing.
Pulse-style 'Describe it' chat on the parked branch jonas/pulse-ui, backed by POST /api/routines/describe; it duplicated the per-routine 'change in your words' box and was undone from main.

workflow: Entire only writes a checkpoint when repo files change; sessions that only read files log 'no files modified, skipping checkpoint', so hooks can look inactive when they fired.
Use separate git worktree folders (ask-soony-pulse, ask-soony-flow) per experimental UI branch and verify with desktop and phone screenshots on a copy of demo state before merging.
Subagents work well for bulk cross-checking (200 order confirmations and 59 scans) and for drawing logo variants without touching the repo.
Before the push, rebase on origin and rerun tests and the build; Entire checks upload checkpoints with the push.
Judges and interviews favor a decision view with pipeline context over a chat; specific questions show the team read the data, general pain questions feed the business case.

friction: The Soony portal token was missing at first, blocking data access until the user filled in .env.
Misread the team's interest in Pulse and built a duplicate chat UI, then had to undo the merge and rebuild as a flow view.
The two-column snake layout read right-to-left on the second row and confused the user; a fix was needed.
The top bar became crowded after adding the role chip, status and heartbeat, needing a 3-column grid and trimmed wording on narrower screens.
The phone action bar overlapped open options and the empty flow layout looked sparse.
Several UI fixes were made right before the 12:00 hand-in with main still unpushed.
Unclear whether portal data and the effects of our emails are the same for all teams.
A portal password ended up in Discord history.
